chapter: Rose Murphy, wartime 52nd Street, Town Hall
title: Irony of Black musicians being drafted for a segregated country
summary: Crouch asks about the irony of Black musicians fighting without full rights; Stewart says it was seldom discussed and calls the war sad.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, now, was there -- sometimes, you know, guys would talk about and I would wonder if guys were talking about it, if you recall any guys talk about it, that it was kind of a ironic situation that what -- that with black musicians having to go through what they were having to go through in the United States' segregated policies and different kinds of exploitation and stuff, that they would have to be inducted in to fight where they might have to risk their lives for a situation in which they weren't actually -- not that -- you know what I'm saying. I mean, it was like they weren't getting their full citizenship rights in a lot of ways, however popular they may have been as entertainers or musicians, you know.
But they were still being demanded (inaudible) everyday --
To go do their duty, yeah.
-- to go over there and stand up in front of those bullets, you know.
Were guys talking about that at all, that it was kind of ironic?
They -- at times, they were, yes.
Do you remember any of the guys who were -- who mentioned that?

Well, not offhand. Of course, my buddy Slim, he mentioned it a few times after he came out of the service, you know. But I might say that on the other hand, the guys didn't talk too much about it, you know. It's just one of those things that they had to do and that was about it. It was a sad thing, in a way, I think, yes.

Well, you just mentioned that when they were inducted into the service, they would have to go over there and face those bullets and what have you. I think the whole affair, as far as I'm concerned, was sad. But, you know, I just felt that way. But in -- let's go back to the Bible. It was said that there will always be war and what have you. So those things are probably meant to be. There is
even war as of today. Some country is at war with another people, what have you. I guess that whole thing goes to make up this whole world.
